title: Baudouin-Desportes to Aldobrandini and to Frachetta, Paris 22 July 1593, BnF fr. 3984 ff. 186, 189

steps.what: Tomokiyo's League polyphonic key and folio list confirm the task is transcription, not key recovery.
f. 188v aligned to its decipherment f. 185: 1,108 labelled glyphs of the same hand.
CNN, kNN, SVM and self-training classifiers read held-out glyphs at 73-79 % top-1; hand reading c. 70 %.
Soft LM decoding of held-out f. 188v ll. 7-10 recovers only 30-40 % of letters.
Line-by-line alignment of f. 186v and f. 189 against the Lisieux text versus a shuffled control: no verbatim shared passage.

Contributed (Paolo Rosson, with Claude Opus 5.5): f. 176 aligned to its decipherment f. 177-178 and f. 188v to f. 185, 6,794 labelled signs; CTC line recogniser; held-out 98.5% of signs, 95.6% of letters; blind test f. 179r 99.7% / 98.3%.
Contributed: Tomokiyo's League key applied with a period-French LM and lexicon decoder to ff. 186 and 189; every line checked on the image by his model; v0.2 published.

Checked here: 1,524 of 1,533 decoded words spell under the key from their sign-class strings (the other 9 use the second-choice class); our 100 hand labels of f. 188v ll. 3-4 agree with his gold on all 100; ff. 186r ll. 21-23 and f. 189 l. 1 re-read glyph by glyph on the Gallica image, every class matches.

Priority: Tomokiyo mayenne.htm (2023) lists both as undeciphered; polyphonic1593.htm (3 Oct 2026) credits Rosson with the first full decipherment; Burford's independent re-reading (18 Oct 2026) agrees on 93-96% of signs and prefers Rosson's text.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked Paolo Rosson's sign-class dumps (rosson/raw/dump_*.txt) as the transcriptions and his readings rosson/f186_reading.txt and rosson/f189_reading.txt as the decryptions; the clear opening of f. 186r (ll. 0-10) is only summarised in his file.

outcome.method_basis: Paolo Rosson applied Tomokiyo's published League polyphonic key (cryptiana mayenne.htm), unchanged, to a transcription made by a recogniser trained on the sister letters aligned with their 1593 decipherments (f. 177-178, f. 184-185); no key was recovered. This project's 17 Sept attempt with the same key stalled at 73-79% of glyphs; its share is the checks of 20 Oct 2026.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Rosson's dumps hold 1,790 cipher words (557 f. 189, 688 f. 186r, 545 f. 186v); his reading files leave 5 unread and mark 21 with (?); 1,764 of 1,790 are read as sense (counted here 20 Oct 2026).

texts.label: f. 186r-v (no. 88), to Pietro Aldobrandini, Paris 22 July 1593
texts.summary: Baudouin-Desportes tells Aldobrandini that the papal commissaries Matteucci and Malvasia did more harm than the enemy, that the Spanish army stayed on the frontier, and that the Legate presses for a king's election just as the enemy wins votes by seeming to turn Catholic and "doit dimanche aller a la messe" (Henri IV heard Mass at Saint-Denis on Sunday 25 July). He recalls his requests in Rome and their refusal; Mayenne was willing to accept Guise as king. Reading by Paolo Rosson (v0.2, 1 Oct 2026) with Tomokiyo's key; the clear opening is only summarised in it.

texts.label: f. 189 (no. 90), to Girolamo Frachetta, July 1593
texts.summary: A letter in cover names ("nostre oncle", "l'homme de la chesne", "l'homme du colege", "nostre docteur Gratian"): the truce is expected "dans peu de jours", an envoy's journey "a fait changer de religion au [roy de Navarre]", and the Legate held back "nos brefz". Reading by Paolo Rosson (v0.2, 1 Oct 2026) with Tomokiyo's key.

prior.where: Paolo Rosson (with Claude Opus 5.5), github.com/pangoleen/desportes-1593, v0.2 of 1 Oct 2026; reported by Tomokiyo (cryptiana polyphonic1593.htm, 3 Oct 2026) and by Brice Dudout's email of 19 Oct 2026. No reading before Rosson's: Tomokiyo's mayenne.htm (2023) and the royal office's register say both letters were undeciphered. Brett Burford's independent re-reading, 18 Oct 2026, followed it.

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue.
